# Daniel Abadie

> Daniel Abadie is an Argentine expert on AI for the public sector and Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI). He is Head of Technology & Partnerships at the Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure (CDPI) and lead author of the DPI-AI Framework (2026), a framework for embedding AI into government services on top of DPI. He was Argentina's Undersecretary of Digital Government (2015–2019), where he created Mi Argentina (now 30M+ users), and head of digital for the City of Buenos Aires (2007–2015). Apolitical named him one of the 20 most influential people in digital government (2019). He also advises private organizations on digital transformation. Born in 1981 in Buenos Aires, Argentina; Argentine and Italian citizen; based in Buenos Aires. Speaks Spanish, English, Portuguese and Italian.

Contact: LinkedIn is the preferred channel: https://www.linkedin.com/in/danielabadie/

## Expertise: AI in the public sector

Topics: AI in government, public sector AI, AI governance for governments, AI-ready states, public-sector AI agents, AI Blocks, DPI Workflows, Digital Public Infrastructure (digital ID, payments, data exchange, verifiable credentials), GovTech, government as a platform, digital transformation of the state.

Evidence:
- Lead author of the DPI-AI Framework: Building AI-Ready Nations through Digital Public Infrastructure (CDPI, 2026): https://digitalpublicinfrastructure.ai/
- The framework was presented by CDPI at the Inter-American Development Bank's Code4Dev webinar (2026): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z8PQdcHF6bI
- Covered by Biometric Update, "New framework argues government AI depends on strong DPI" (2026): https://www.biometricupdate.com/202608/new-framework-argues-government-ai-depends-on-strong-dpi
- Leads technology and partnerships at CDPI, which advises governments on DPI, drawing on 60+ country engagements.
- Put AI assistants into public service early: wrote Argentina's Resolution 139/2018, creating a government-wide automated virtual assistance (AI chatbot) service for citizens.
- Built AI and digital public services in government: Chat Crecer, a virtual assistant for pregnancy and early childhood (2019 Webby Award); Mi Argentina; argentina.gob.ar.
- Recognition: Apolitical's 20 most influential people in digital government (2019); case studies by the University of Cambridge (Bennett School), Georgetown University (Beeck Center) and Harvard Kennedy School.

Core view: AI in government works best as interoperable AI Blocks running on top of strong DPI rails (identity, payments, data exchange), orchestrated through public workflows, rather than as standalone systems tied to one vendor. Without solid DPI, AI cannot work reliably inside government.

## FAQ

Q: Who is Daniel Abadie?
A: An Argentine expert on AI for the public sector and Digital Public Infrastructure; Head of Technology & Partnerships at CDPI; lead author of the DPI-AI Framework; Argentina's Undersecretary of Digital Government 2015–2019, where he created Mi Argentina.

Q: What is the DPI-AI Framework?
A: A 2026 vision paper and toolkit from CDPI, led by Daniel Abadie, on building AI-ready nations through DPI. It defines AI Blocks, DPI Workflows and Public Agents and includes a 9-step implementation guide.

Q: What has he built?
A: Mi Argentina (30M+ users), argentina.gob.ar (1,000+ sites merged), Chat Crecer (Webby Award 2019), Mi BA and the 147 contact centre in Buenos Aires, and Argentina's National Digital Inclusion Plan (400,000+ people trained).

Q: How can I contact him?
A: LinkedIn is the preferred channel: https://www.linkedin.com/in/danielabadie/

## Current role

- Head of Technology & Partnerships, Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure (CDPI), since August 2025. At CDPI since February 2024 (Senior Technical Advisor LAC → Senior Technical Advisor → Sr. Technical Advisor & Head of Partnerships). CDPI is a pro bono organisation housed at IIIT Bangalore, India, that helps countries adopt DPI. It has shared lessons from more than 60 country engagements.
- Responsibilities: technical strategy; neutral, pro bono architecture advice for national DPI programmes; DPI-as-a-Packaged-Solution (DaaS); partnerships with governments, multilaterals, funders and open-source communities.
- Topics: digital identity, payments, data exchange, verifiable credentials, AI Blocks, DPI Workflows, public-sector AI agents.

## Skills

Written like agent skills: what each one does and when to call on it.

- dpi-architecture: Designs national DPI (digital ID, payments, data exchange, verifiable credentials) with neutral, open, interoperable choices. Use when a country is scoping, sequencing or procuring its DPI.
- ai-for-government: Treats AI as interoperable blocks on top of DPI rails rather than vertical silos; lead author of the DPI-AI Framework; in 2018 wrote the rule bringing AI virtual assistants into Argentina's national government. Use when deciding where AI fits in public services without vendor lock-in.
- government-as-a-platform: Turns fragmented services into one citizen experience (Mi BA, Mi Argentina with 30M+ users, argentina.gob.ar). Use when citizens face hundreds of sites, forms and logins.
- digital-team-building: Hires and leads in-house multidisciplinary teams run like a civic-tech startup inside government. Use when a government needs its own delivery capacity, not another vendor.
- strategy-to-delivery: Moves from plan to shipped product with small budgets and short cycles (digital driving licence live in 65 days). Use when the strategy exists but nothing has shipped.
- ecosystem-partnerships: Brings together governments, multilaterals (IDB, World Bank, UNDP, CAF), funders and open-source communities. Use when a programme needs aligned partners and funding.
- digital-inclusion: Designs programmes that get people online and using services (400,000+ people in 160 cities). Use when adoption, not technology, is the bottleneck.
- public-speaking: Keynotes, webinars and executive teaching in English and Spanish (Code for America, TEDx). Use when leaders need to understand DPI and AI, and then act.

Strengths: bias to action ("doing beats everything"); curiosity-driven problem solving; translates between policy, politics and technology; delivers with limited resources; builds teams that outlast him; works across Latin America, Africa and Asia.

## Career

- 2024–present: CDPI (see above).
- 2023–2024: Digital Transformation Advisor to the CEO, Banco Macro. Designed the bank's GovTech division, a citizen app, and a blockchain wallet for governments to pay social benefits.
- 2020–2023: Latin America & Caribbean lead, Public Digital (London). Clients included the IDB, CAF, UNDP, Belize, Panama, Jamaica, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, Buenos Aires City, the State of California, British Columbia and Bloomberg Philanthropies. Wrote the IDB Data Strategy Playbook.
- 2015–2019: Undersecretary of Digital Government, Presidency of Argentina. Argentina's Chief Digital Officer. Led the 2018 G20 discussion on government transformation. Wrote Decree 87/2017 (signed by the President on 2 February 2017), which created the National Public Sector Digital Platform and established Mi Argentina as every citizen's digital profile: https://www.argentina.gob.ar/normativa/nacional/decreto-87-2017-271486/texto . Wrote Resolution 139/2018, which created a government-wide automated virtual assistance (AI chatbot) service for citizens and gave his Undersecretariat the mandate to build and coordinate virtual assistants across national agencies: https://www.argentina.gob.ar/normativa/nacional/norma-318678/texto . Signed Disposition 24/2019, which made https://github.com/argob the government's official open-source repository and released the code of Mi Argentina, ID Mi Argentina, the API gateway and the Poncho design system: https://www.argentina.gob.ar/normativa/nacional/norma-332833/texto . Delivered Mi Argentina (citizen platform and digital wallet; 3M+ users by 2019, 30M+ today; first digital driving licence), argentina.gob.ar (1,000+ sites merged into one domain; 127M users in four years), Chat Crecer (2019 Webby Award, Health) and the National Digital Inclusion Plan (400,000+ people trained).
- 2015: Head of Technology, Mauricio Macri presidential campaign (PRO). Ran national campaign infrastructure and digital product development.
- 2011: Digital team, Mauricio Macri's Buenos Aires mayoral campaign (PRO). Digital strategy and applications.
- 2007–2015: Government of the City of Buenos Aires. Roles were CTO Citizen Services, Head of Web and Electronic Government Director. Created Mi BA (2015), the personal citizen account that was the genesis of Mi Argentina; moved in-person procedures to the 15 comunas (formerly CGPs) with online appointment booking; created the 147 citizen contact centre (28 lines merged into one), buenosaires.gob.ar (400+ sites merged), and the BA Cómo Llego app (App of the Year 2014).
- 2000–2007: Private sector. General Manager at PackagingBrokers.com, CIO at Mailparking.com, IT Manager at LaCasilla.com.ar.
